renderReview.method: owner inspected the live world at player-eye cameras and rejected it for style coherence; culling follows from the named hard fails
notes: The snowy-pine idea is abandoned: Frost Hollow's identity now comes from the biome bible (cool stone cliffs, deep desaturated foliage, violet crystals, snow caps) rather than from a differently-textured tree, because a textured tree is exactly what cannot be tinted into a biome.
Rocks skew pale. They are tinted WARM in the canyon and cool in the hollow, which the builder now does through the biome rather than through a per-call-site argument.

The fence enclosure that the previous review rejected is now culled from the palette outright rather than special-cased at one call site; the prospector's corral is built from two runs of the kept panel.

curation.trigger: Owner pixel review rejected the art pass: 'the world reads too much like multiple unrelated free assets placed into one map'. 26 assets acquired is not 26 assets that must remain — a smaller coherent palette beats a larger incoherent one.
curation.target: roughly 3 tree assets, 2-3 rock, 1-2 bush, one coherent fence/sign set, one coherent prop set
curation.outcome: 26 -> 15. Four trees across two silhouette classes (two slim pines, two round), three rocks in one proportion band, the one bush, three crystals in a 2.7-4.7 width band at 8 studs, ONE fence panel, ONE signpost, two cube crates.
curation.whyFourTreesNotThree: Three tree assets would leave one of the two silhouette classes with a single member, and 'essentially one repeated tree family' is a named failure condition from the first review. Four across two classes is the smallest palette that clears both the coherence complaint and the repetition one.
criteria: TINTABLE: a mesh carrying a TextureID cannot be recoloured (MeshPart.Color has no effect), so it cannot be painted into a biome. Assets whose names assert a baked texture are culled outright; the builder additionally measures TextureID at load and refuses untintable members in any biome their texture does not already suit.

PROPORTION BAND: members of a family must sit in one width band at the family's normalised height. A member two or three times the footprint of its siblings is the mechanism behind 'trees, rocks, fences, crates disagree strongly in scale'.
ONE OBJECT PER ROLE: one fence design, one signpost design. A second design in the same role is what makes a world read as assembled from a catalogue.
SILHOUETTE ADDS A READ: a third cube crate the same size as two cube crates adds a member and no information.
curation.enforcement: The allowlist is duplicated in world/Build.luau (CURATED) and is authoritative there. If the cull lived only in this file, a re-run of the asset broker would quietly put the culled assets back into ServerStorage and back into the world. The builder excludes anything not on the allowlist and NAMES it in the build summary, so an unvetted new acquisition is visible rather than silent.

culled.name: Quartz Crystal Cluster
culled.reason: 6.7 wide against the kept crystals' tight 2.7-4.7 band at the same 8-stud height. A formation mixing it reads as two different crystal species rather than one seam.

culled.name: Very Low-poly mountain rock thing
culled.reason: 13.9 x 16.1 at 5 studs tall is a flat plate, not a boulder — roughly three times the footprint of the kept rocks at the same height, so a scatter mixing them has no consistent rock scale.

culled.name: low poly tree
culled.reason: A 12.3 x 20.2 footprint at 30 tall. The lopsided plan reads as a different species from every other tree in the world, and from above it reads as a modelling error.

culled.name: Tree
culled.reason: 29.8 wide at 30 tall — a spreading canopy with more than twice the footprint of the other round trees at the same height. The clearest single contributor to 'trees, rocks, fences, crates disagree strongly in scale'.

culled.name: Wood Crate (1x1x1)
culled.reason: A third cube crate at the same 4-stud size as the two kept. Redundant silhouette — it adds a member without adding a read.

culled.name: LOWPOLYCRATE
culled.reason: 9.7 x 7.8 at 4 studs tall is a pallet, not a crate: a different object at a different scale sharing a family with two cubes, which is how a 'crate stack' ends up looking like two unrelated props.

culled.name: Sign
culled.reason: A bare 0.6-deep board with no post. The kept 'Wooden Sign' has a post and shares the fence's wooden vocabulary; a post-less floating board was part of why signs read as unstyled imported meshes.

culled.name: fence.gate.open
culled.reason: A GATE, not a fence panel: 7.4 studs deep against a panel's 0.2. The world already has one authored gate, and a second gate-shaped object threaded into a fence run is the 'unrelated free assets placed into one map' read in miniature.

culled.name: Meshes/fence (1)
culled.reason: A second fence design (7.2 x 7 x 0.7 against the kept panel's 11.6 x 7 x 0.2). Two fence designs in one world is one too many; a fence run should be one fence.

culled.name: Pine-Tree-Tex
culled.reason: Its name asserts a baked texture, and MeshPart.Color has no effect where TextureID is set: it can be neither warmed for the canyon nor cooled for the hollow, so it stands in whatever palette its author baked. The single most likely source of the 'bright lime-green tree inside the snow biome' hard fail.

culled.name: text.pine
culled.reason: Textured by name, with the same untintable problem; and 32.4 wide against 34 tall is a squat blob whose silhouette disagrees with the two slim pines kept.
